title: The prayer as rest
hook: the Prophet ﷺ said: give us rest by it, Bilal (Abu Dawud)

segments.voice: Yesterday, khushu', presence in prayer, and your line: know what you say. Was there one word in one prayer that you actually heard yourself say? Today, the last day on the prayer, and the end of a week. Day one thousand ninety-two.

A man is sitting with a few people, and he says out loud that he wishes he had prayed, so he could have found some rest. The people around him seem to think that's an odd thing to say, and they let him know it. Rest? Prayer is a duty. You get it done. So he answers them with something he heard the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ say. The report is in the Sunan of Abu Dawud. The Prophet ﷺ would turn to Bilal, the man who called the prayer, and say: Bilal, call the iqamah, and give us rest by it. Not rest after it. Rest by it. Today, the prayer as the place you put things down.
screen: `I WISH I HAD PRAYED, AND RESTED.` → `REST? IT'S A DUTY.` → `BILAL, GIVE US REST BY IT.`

segments.voice: Start with the Arabic the report gives: arihna biha. Give us rest by it, or with it. Some teachers point at that small word, biha, by it. There is a way of praying that sounds like the opposite: give us rest from it, let's get this over with. The words in the report go the other way. The prayer isn't the task standing between you and your rest. It is the rest. Second, the prayer isn't the only place this idea shows up. The Qur'an puts it plainly in surah thirteen, in Pickthall's words: "Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!" The prayer is remembrance in a body: standing, bowing, putting the forehead on the ground. Another report, in the Sunan of an-Nasa'i, has the Prophet ﷺ say that the comfort of his eye was placed in the prayer. Comfort of the eye is an Arabic way of saying the thing you're glad to look at, the thing that settles you. Third, look back at this week, because it has been building to this. The Friday sermon, heard in silence. The lighter prayer on the road. Two prostrations when you forget, because mistakes are expected. One prostration of thanks at good news. A prayer for every kind of sky. And yesterday, knowing what you say. Each of those makes the prayer a little less like a test you pass and a little more like a room you walk into. Fourth, an ordinary day. Several times a day the world stops asking you for things for a few minutes. The inbox can wait. For Muslims, that pause is required, and the report says it was meant to feel like relief, not like one more thing on the list. That's where these days on the prayer end: not with a rule, but with the Prophet ﷺ asking Bilal to call the iqamah, so they could rest.
screen: `ARIHNA BIHA: GIVE US REST BY IT.` · `IN REMEMBRANCE, HEARTS FIND REST.` · `THIS WEEK, BUILDING TO REST.` · `A ROOM YOU WALK INTO.` · then, large: `VERILY IN THE REMEMBRANCE OF ALLAH DO HEARTS FIND REST!`

segments.voice: The practice: pray to rest, not to finish. If you pray, take your next prayer slowly, and in each position, standing, bowing, prostrating, let one thing you're carrying go down with you. If you don't pray, sit now and do the same with your breath. Breathe in, and notice what you're holding: a task, a worry, a conversation. Breathe out, and set it on the floor beside you, just for these two minutes. You don't have to finish anything. The bell holds the time.
The prayer as rest. Arihna biha: give us rest by it. The Prophet's words to Bilal, and the close of the prayer. Today's word.

Your line: rest in it. Today, the next time you stop for anything, a prayer, a coffee, a red light, treat it as rest rather than a delay. Tomorrow, a new pillar: zakat, and a word that means two things at once. Day one thousand ninety-two.

howItsDone: Muslims pray the daily prayers, and teachers sometimes recall the Prophet's words to Bilal, 'give us rest by it,' to encourage praying unhurried, as a relief rather than a chore.

fork.setup: it's time to pray, and the Prophet ﷺ turns to Bilal. what does the report say he asks for?
options: call it quickly, so we can be done with it.
call the iqamah, and give us rest by it.
wait until we have finished our work.
fork.reveal: give us rest by it. the prayer isn't the thing between him and rest; it's where the rest is.

original.note: Arabic: give us rest by it, the Prophet's words to Bilal about the prayer (Abu Dawud).

trapdoor: what you thought: prayer is one more task to get through.
what it means: the Prophet ﷺ asked Bilal to call the prayer so they could rest by it.
what a scholar hears: biha, by it, not minha, from it; teachers use that small difference to describe two ways of praying.

sources.quoted: Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!

notes: Abu Dawud 4985: confirm number, the framing (a man wishing he had prayed and found rest, others objecting), and the grading.
Nasa'i 3939 ('the comfort of my eye was placed in prayer'): confirm number; some editions number it 3940.
Pickthall 13:28 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording and punctuation.
'biha, not minha' is presented as a point some teachers make, not as a textual variant; confirm Keeper is comfortable with it.

Editor: removed 'in Medina' (the report gives no place), fixed the close (the Prophet asked Bilal, not 'a man his friend'), 'one letter's difference' (biha/minha differ by more than a letter), and varied the stock 'ordinary Tuesday' line.
